terra.problem: The coffee in the joke breaks the food rule.
The verse does not say nobody will come from Egypt.
The claim about Egypt appearing often in the Bible refers beyond the passage without a reference.
The explanation is a flat restatement followed by generic reading advice.
The reference to how the book started reaches outside the passage without a reference to Hosea 1:9.
The verse does mention family roles: wife and husband.
The LORD is not identified as the speaker before the quote in which He says “I.”
The verse says she thought this, not that she said it. The following verses also do not identify the LORD as the giver of every item on her list, such as water.
The verse does not place thorns on one side and a wall on the other.
The verse says she will say she will return; it does not say she actually heads back.
The explanation says she is heading back and turning back, but the verse says only what she will say she will do.
The verse says she does not acknowledge the LORD as the giver; it does not say she never acknowledged Him.
The verse says the silver and gold were crafted for Baal, not that she gave Baal credit for the gifts.
The explanation is mechanical and generic, with little of Papa Dorin's voice.
The passage does not say she was counting on her lovers to deliver her from the LORD's hands.
The verse does not say the trees stood in a neat row.
The cookie-tray comparison does not match the action in the passage and makes light of the LORD's stated judgment.
